sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006)

contents.name: §4.2: perfect-fluid stress tensor and observer energy

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete rest-frame perfect-fluid reduction and the moving-observer energy formula in §4.2, PDF pp. 14–15.
source_review.supports: The isotropic perfect stress form and the distinction between rest-frame energy density and a moving observer projection.
source_review.limitations: The adopted postulate fixes its own -+++ and SI conventions and is a selected model, not a claim that all matter is perfect-fluid matter.

contents.name: §4.3: supplied equation of state, rest energy and first-law derivatives

source_review.read_extent: Read §4.3 from the assumed local equation of state and rest-mass term (4.10)–(4.11), through fixed-comoving-volume first law (4.12)–(4.13) and derivative definitions (4.14), PDF pp. 15–17.
source_review.supports: A supplied rest-frame state function includes rest energy; temperature and chemical potentials are state derivatives; the comoving parcel differential has pressure work when volume varies.
source_review.limitations: The source uses multiple species and c=1 chemical-potential notation. The local item specifies one fixed-composition C2 state function, restores SI units, and proves its own calculus conditionally.

contents.name: §§5.1–5.4: perfect stress balance projections and entropy identity

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete local conservation and perfect-fluid projection argument, including energy/particle balance and entropy reduction, PDF pp. 17–20.
source_review.supports: Under the source’s perfect-fluid balances and thermodynamic identities, the energy equation yields local entropy-current conservation and entropy per particle advection.
source_review.limitations: The physics theorem consumes the exact current draft mathematical supplier rather than treating the source as proof acceptance; its conclusion remains conditional on the model and current supplier.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Carter–Lichnerowicz development through the material-loop circulation discussion and the isentropic specialization, PDF pp. 20–24.
source_review.supports: The enthalpy-vorticity identity retains an entropy-gradient source; the isentropic restriction removes that source under spatially constant entropy per particle.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem uses the exact current draft circulation lemma and states local compact-loop conditions; it does not infer global conservation from advective constancy alone.

sources.title: Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (version of 2 September 2015)
sources.locator: Full 184-page PDF; §I.1.3, PDF pp. 4–5, and §§IX.1–IX.3.2, PDF pp. 134–148.

contents.name: §I.1.3: local thermodynamic equilibrium as a continuum-model premise

source_review.read_extent: Read §I.1.3 in full, including its small-cell local-equilibrium condition and state-function interpretation, PDF pp. 4–5.
source_review.supports: Local thermodynamic equilibrium is an explicit modeling assumption for a continuum cell, not a consequence of the balance equations.
source_review.limitations: The adopted branch supplies its own C2 function and limited regime; it does not assert a universal thermodynamic-limit EOS or microscopic derivation.

contents.name: §§IX.1–IX.3.1: relativistic marker current and perfect stress tensor

source_review.read_extent: Read the conservation-equation statements, four-velocity/local-rest-frame definition, and full arbitrary-frame perfect current/stress formulas, PDF pp. 134–147.
source_review.supports: An isolated perfect-fluid model uses a convective particle four-current and an isotropic stress-energy tensor built from the metric, pressure, energy density and unit flow.
source_review.limitations: The local postulate specifies the current, conventions and smooth regime; the source’s formulation is used for independent model context, not as empirical validation.

contents.name: §IX.3.2: entropy-current conservation and entropy per particle

source_review.read_extent: Read the full displayed derivation of entropy-current conservation and its continuity-equation consequence, PDF pp. 148–149.
source_review.supports: The source obtains entropy conservation conditionally from perfect-fluid energy-momentum conservation, particle conservation and its Gibbs–Duhem identity.
source_review.limitations: The consuming proof uses the exact mathematical supplier’s current interface and proof status; no source citation certifies that draft supplier.

sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006)
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF; §4.2, PDF pp. 14–15, including equations (4.6)–(4.9).

contents.name: §4.2: perfect stress and energy assigned to a moving observer

source_review.read_extent: Read the rest-frame stress-energy and complete moving-observer contraction calculation in §4.2, PDF pp. 14–15.
source_review.supports: A perfect stress has rest energy density and isotropic pressure; a moving observer’s projected energy density depends on the relative Lorentz factor.
source_review.limitations: The local example independently contracts the tensor and describes only a prescribed Minkowski background, not Einstein backreaction or an observation.

sources.title: Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (version of 2 September 2015)

contents.name: §§IX.2–IX.3.1: local rest flow and arbitrary-frame perfect stress

source_review.read_extent: Read the unit four-velocity/local-rest-frame definition and the perfect particle current and stress-energy tensor in arbitrary coordinates and frames, PDF pp. 137–147.
source_review.supports: The perfect tensor/current have explicit observer and frame conventions from which the constant-state boost calculation can be checked.
source_review.limitations: The example fixes dimensionless unit observers and derives its own contraction; the source’s unit notation is not silently adopted.
